method: colour of the tapetum lucidum noted in the Results description of the eye in the fixed heads (10% buffered formalin, evaluated 48 h later); the paper does not say how many animals or eyes the tapetum statement rests on, nor whether it was seen in fresh tissue, in sections or by ophthalmoscopy
conditions: Heads of five adult crab-eating foxes (three female, two male) from CETAS-IBAMA Salvador/BA (a triage centre for wild animals) and the Department of Anatomy, EMEVZ/UFBA; the animals had died of natural causes and the heads had no compromised bone or sense organs. One further live adult male (5.5 kg) was scanned by CT under anaesthesia and returned to CETAS; no fundus or tapetum finding is attributed to it. source.authors: Ingrid van der Merwe, Ákos Lukáts, Veronika Bláhová, Maria K. Oosthuizen, Nigel C. Bennett, Pavel Němec
source.title: The topography of rods, cones and intrinsically photosensitive retinal ganglion cells in the retinas of a nocturnal (Micaelamys namaquensis) and a diurnal (Rhabdomys pumilio) rodent

method: immunocytochemistry on whole-mounted retina (rods labelled with the rhodopsin antibody Rho4D2); topographical density map; the Abstract gives the peak as approximate (~)
conditions: Adult wild-caught Namaqua rock mice (Micaelamys namaquensis) from Goro Game Reserve, Soutpansberg, Limpopo Province, South Africa; animals perfused transcardially with 0.9% saline then 4% paraformaldehyde (some with Zamboni's fixative). The paper does not state how many M. namaquensis animals were used; it says one whole retina per species was used for the analysis of each photoreceptor type (so each density is from a single retina). Whole retinae were mounted in aqueous medium; the paper's only shrinkage statement concerns cones (cone densities were not corrected for shrinkage because shrinkage was negligible in whole retinae mounted in the aqueous medium), and it says nothing about shrinkage or its correction for rod densities. Rods were counted from one 117 x 88 um photograph per 1 mm2 grid square at 1000x. The comparison species in the same paper, the four-striped field mouse (Rhabdomys pumilio), came from a laboratory breeding colony and is not filed here. The Results section gives the rod density range for this species as 20712 to 81088 rods/mm2 and states no distinct centro-peripheral gradient in M. namaquensis; the overall mean rod density was 50820 rods/mm2 for the nocturnal species. The Abstract sentence also gives the R. pumilio peak (~84467/mm2), its central value (~56618/mm2) and its peripheral value (~32689/mm2); only the M. namaquensis peak is filed.
quote: Similar rod density peaks were observed (R. pumilio: ~84467/mm2; M. namaquensis: ~81088/mm2), but a density gradient yielded higher values in the central (~56618/mm2) rather than in the peripheral retinal region (~32689/mm2) in R. pumilio.
note: New trait: rod_density_mm2 is a key already on main (rabbit rows and desk-d243's Bolinichthys longipes row) though absent from the checker list. Value is the sentence's own M. namaquensis figure; the quote names the species in its own clause. source.title: The topography of rods, cones and intrinsically photosensitive retinal ganglion cells in the retinas of a nocturnal (Micaelamys namaquensis) and a diurnal (Rhabdomys pumilio) rodent

method: immunocytochemistry on whole-mounted retina (S-opsin and M/L-opsin cones); overall mean over the retina
conditions: Adult wild-caught Namaqua rock mice (Micaelamys namaquensis) from Goro Game Reserve, Soutpansberg, Limpopo Province, South Africa; animals perfused transcardially with 0.9% saline then 4% paraformaldehyde (some with Zamboni's fixative). The paper does not state how many M. namaquensis animals were used; it says one whole retina per species was used for the analysis of each photoreceptor type (so each density is from a single retina). Whole retinae were mounted in aqueous medium and the authors state shrinkage was negligible, so densities were not corrected for it. The comparison species in the same paper, the four-striped field mouse (Rhabdomys pumilio), came from a laboratory breeding colony and is not filed here. The sentence gives the all-cone overall mean; the paper separates S-cones and M/L-cones elsewhere (S- to M/L-cone ratio about 1:7.8 in M. namaquensis, stated in the Abstract) and the cone-to-rod ratio of 1:12.4. The peak cone density (both cone types counted) is about 5766/mm2, already cited in the note of main's sweep-86 receptor_classes row for this species, and is not in the quoted sentence. In M. namaquensis both cone populations show a centro-peripheral density gradient, so the overall mean averages over that gradient; M/L-cone densities range from 2018 to 5066/mm2 and S-cone densities from 151 to 800/mm2. Cones were counted from one 117 x 88 um photograph per 1 mm2 grid square at 1000x.
quote: The overall mean cone density was almost 8 times higher in R. pumilio (31640 cones/mm2) than in M. namaquensis (4113 cones/mm2).

(31640 cones/mm2)' | 'than in M. namaquensis (4113 cones/mm2).'), final period seen. The one sentence supports two species; the M. namaquensis value (4113) stands in its own clause and the R. pumilio value (31640, laboratory-bred) is not filed. source.authors: Graham R. Martin, Kerry-Jayne Wilson, J. Martin Wild, Stuart Parsons, M. Fabiana Kubke, Jeremy Corfield
source.title: Kiwi Forego Vision in the Guidance of Their Nocturnal Activities

method: eye dimensions from post mortem specimens; the sentence gives one figure for axial length and equatorial diameter together; the paper does not say whether the eyes were measured fresh or fixed, nor whether the figure is a mean of the two eyes or a range
conditions: Post mortem specimens of North Island brown kiwi (Apteryx mantelli) collected at Keri Keri, New Zealand under Department of Conservation permits; the paper does not say whether the birds were wild or captive, their age or sex, or how long after death the eyes were measured. 'The two Kiwi eyes sampled' means two eyes (the paper does not say whether from one or two birds; the same post mortem material gave n = 2 kiwi brains, fixed by immersion in 4% paraformaldehyde, and no fixation or measuring method is stated for the eyes). The same paper's visual-field measurements (monocular field 125 degrees, binocular field almost non-existent) were made on two live captive adults, one A. mantelli and one A. haastii, and are already on main. The sentence after this one says overall eye shape resembled diurnal birds such as the common starling and rock pigeon; the paper concludes that kiwi forgo vision in guiding nocturnal activities, an anatomical inference with no behavioural vision tests. The Discussion says kiwi eye size falls well outside the uniform scaling of eye diameter with body mass in birds.
quote: Axial length and equatorial diameter of the two Kiwi eyes sampled = 7.0 mm.
note: New trait for this species: eye_axial_length_mm is a key already on main (absent from the checker list). Whole Results sentence (13 words), read intact in a second pass (no preceding sentence in the paragraph; followed by 'Overall eye shape was similar to that of diurnally active birds...'). Value is the printed 7.0 mm, which the sentence assigns to axial length and equatorial diameter alike.
